te: Following births registered with a false father, with the Department of Provincial Administration and Bangkok
se: The committee invited the Department of Provincial Administration and the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration to give information on births of children whose mothers are foreigners but whose fathers were falsely named as Thai. It heard the steps for registering a birth within 15 days and the documents used. Bangkok reported that it has checked the past 10 years and set preventive measures, such as checks of past records at every district office, a register of birth notifications, rotating staff and a queue system. The committee suggested using blood group results as a first screen before DNA tests, and clearer penalties for giving false information. It also approved in principle the policy proposals and 8 urgent measures on school safety from the subcommittee on children after the school shooting in Nonthaburi, and approved in principle a working group to study enforcing the law to prevent the use of kratom drinks mixed with other substances.

te: Results of the Krabi visit on women's roles, and the work of the subcommittees on children and older persons
se: The committee summed up the visit to Krabi (25–26 Jul 2026) on strengthening women and their roles. Proposals included letting people who inspire their communities lead, promoting job skills and products with local identity, promoting products by persons with disabilities as a separate OTOP group, and choosing community products for online channels. It noted that the subcommittee on children will present its report on early childhood development by local government to the Senate on 1 Sep 2026, and that the subcommittee on older persons will hold the forum “Volunteers Bringing Children to School” and summed up its visits to Chachoengsao and Chon Buri, which found problems such as budgets for repairing buildings, a lack of carers for persons with disabilities and food allowances that no longer match today's costs. It also planned a study of kratom drinks mixed with other substances and took up cases of births registered with a false father.

te: Studying the 2027 budget of the Social Development ministry, and kratom drinks mixed with other substances among young people
se: The committee studied the Budget Expenditure Bill for fiscal year 2027 for the Ministry of Social Development and Human Security, with information from the Parliamentary Budget Office. Its observations included building one complete database of people covering welfare, education and health, reviewing overlapping projects and setting quality-of-life indicators. It noted the schedule of the ad hoc budget committee (the ministry's budget from 22 Jul and the Community Development Department's from 11 Aug 2026) and took up for further study the spread of kratom drinks mixed with other substances, which affects the health and safety of children and youth.

te: Results of the visits to Lamphun (ethnic communities) and Phang Nga (livelihood groups and women's networks)
se: The committee summed up the visit to Lamphun (26–27 Jun 2026), which discussed protecting ethnic groups' ways of life, recognising rights to live and farm in traditional ways, the effect of the burning ban on rotational farming, phone and internet signals, and school buildings in the Pa Pae area, and visited a weaving group and the Karen children and youth council. It agreed that community-based tourism and market channels should be promoted. It then summed up the visit to Phang Nga (2–4 Jul 2026), to community enterprise groups that use local wisdom to make a living, and talks with agencies and women's networks on using community mechanisms to watch for, prevent and help those affected.

te: Pride Month forum “The Law and the Future of LGBTQ”, and a seminar on the employment law for older persons
se: The committee reviewed the forum “The Law and the Future of LGBTQ” held in Pride month (25 Jun 2026) with King Prajadhipok's Institute, the National Health Commission Office, the Department of Women's Affairs and Family Development and civil society. It had panel talks and 4 group discussions: health and family; rights, justice and education; the Gender Equality Act B.E. 2015 (2015); and labour and the economy. The proposals will be used to follow up and recommend laws and policies to the government. The committee also approved in principle an academic seminar, “The Law on Employment Security for Older Persons: Assessment and Directions for Reform”.

te: Schedule of the Phang Nga visit, and the work of the subcommittees
se: The committee considered the schedule of the field visit to Phang Nga (2–4 Jul 2026) to follow work on children, youth, women, older persons, persons with disabilities, the disadvantaged and ethnic groups. It followed progress of all 3 subcommittees and noted the work of committee members serving on ad hoc committees considering bills, such as the draft Local Personnel Administration Act.

te: Preparing for the 2027 budget: food for children and school lunches
se: The committee noted announcements, such as a letter asking for help with the way of life of the Karen community of Ban Phu Men and a seminar on the economy and hosting WorldPride 2030. It then prepared information for considering the Budget Expenditure Bill for fiscal year 2027 in the social area: an honorary adviser presented food costs for children in units of the Department of Children and Youth and local government subsidies for school lunches, stressing enough funding and nutrition standards, and an analysis of the Ministry of Social Development and Human Security's budget against social results. It also noted progress from committee members working on other committees.

te: Early childhood report with 7 proposals, such as one data system per child and local government as the first door
se: The committee approved postponing the visits to the Karen community of Ban Phu Men, Uthai Thani, and Ban Doi Chang Pa Pae, Lamphun, and extended the ethnic groups working group by 60 days. It considered the report on promoting the role of local government in early childhood development, which has 7 proposals, such as one early-childhood data system so that no child is missed, local government as the place to receive and refer cases, linking local government, sub-district health promoting hospitals, schools and child development centres, special services for vulnerable children, and making investment in early childhood a national agenda. It also confirmed the volunteer role models from 58 provinces and 11 put forward by the committee (results 30 Jun, awards 18 Aug 2026).

te: Contest awards given; meetings planned with the Social Development and Interior ministers, and a Phang Nga visit
se: The committee noted the award ceremony of the video contest “Echoes of Hope for the Future of Thai Society” (12 May 2026, 80 people attended). It prepared to meet the Deputy Minister of Interior (in charge of the Community Development Department) on 21 May and the Minister of Social Development and Human Security on 27 May 2026 to discuss social policy and laws with the new Council of Ministers, and prepared a field visit to Phang Nga (2–4 Jul 2026) on children, women, older persons, persons with disabilities and ethnic groups.

te: Young children and local government, ethnic groups, a Pride Month forum and disabled parking at Parliament
se: The committee noted the work of all 3 subcommittees. The subcommittee on children is preparing a report on the role of local government in early childhood development, following the ethnic groups law, and framing work on young people not in education or work (NEET), children's mental health, violence against children and children dropping out of school. The subcommittee on women is preparing the forum “The Law and the Future of LGBTQ” in Pride month and a field visit to Phang Nga on domestic violence. The subcommittee on older persons is studying education for persons with disabilities, technology for older persons, facilities and parking for persons with disabilities at Parliament House, and the project “Volunteers Bringing Children to School”. The committee also noted the date of the contest award ceremony (12 May 2026).

te: Rules for choosing “Senate Role Models Doing Good for the Nation”
se: The committee considered nominations for the project “Senate Role Models Doing Good for the Nation: Volunteers Who Create Value and Inspire Society”. A role model should volunteer for society over a long time, have knowledge and skills that benefit others, and have good morals and ethics. Each province sends 1 name by 15 May 2026; the committee chooses special awards by 29 May; results are announced on 30 Jun and awards given on 18 Aug 2026 at Parliament House.
it: Senate Role Models Doing Good for the Nation: rules and timetable

te: The new chair sets the next steps: video contest, role models, a livelihoods fair and assessing laws
se: At the first meeting with Mr. Porthai Montri as chair, the committee set its next steps: the award ceremony of the video contest (12 May 2026), the project “Senate Role Models Doing Good for the Nation” (awards on 18 Aug 2026), the third Senate Joining Forces jobs, livelihoods and market fair, and the work of the 3 working groups assessing laws with King Prajadhipok's Institute and the Westminster Foundation for Democracy, following the principle of leaving no one behind. It also appointed a chief adviser and honorary advisers to the committee.

te: A new chair of the committee, and the rights of ethnic groups
se: Mrs. Varapas Phaiphannarat asked to resign as chair of the committee. The meeting elected Mr. Prathueang Montri (now listed in the Senate directory as Mr. Porthai Montri) as chair. It assigned committee members to serve on ad hoc committees and the Senate ethics committee, filled the vacant vice-chair and secretary posts, and noted the work of the subcommittees, such as enforcing the Act on the Protection and Promotion of Ethnic Groups' Ways of Life B.E. 2025 (2025) (the Department of National Parks, the Royal Forest Department, the Department of Provincial Administration and other agencies invited) and the role of women in preventing domestic violence.

te: Information for the government's social policy, and protecting children from online media
se: The committee noted the results of the video contest (award ceremony 12 May 2026). It gathered information from all 3 subcommittees for the social part of the Council of Ministers' policy statement and sent it to the Office of the National Economic and Social Development Council. It discussed with a representative of King Prajadhipok's Institute measures to protect children and youth when they use online media, looking at Indonesia's rule that children under 16 may not have accounts on high-risk digital platforms.

te: Working groups to assess 3 laws, and proposals on education for autistic persons
se: The committee approved the results of the team category of the video contest (announced 30 Mar 2026) and appointed 3 working groups to review laws after they take effect: the law on preventing and solving domestic violence against children and women, the law promoting employment and quality of life of older persons, and the law promoting the rights of people of diverse genders and their access to public services. It considered 6 proposals from the Autism Parents Association (Thailand) on education for autistic persons and people with special needs and passed them to the subcommittee on persons with disabilities to take forward. It also prepared the Senate jobs, livelihoods and market fair project.
